correctness.rationale: For every fixed integer m>=2, the small-rate entropy expansion follows from the exact Poisson max masses and a uniformly controlled tail. The log-Poisson mass identity has expectation-level Stirling control under both the parent and maximum. The distribution-function term converges with a uniform logarithmic integrability bound. Gaussian Poincare is strict for a nonaffine maximum and normal maximum entropy proves the exact negative high-rate constant. Continuity gives at least one crossover; the checker confirms representative values without substituting for proof.

value.rationale: Replicated count maxima occur in event surveillance and extremal measurements. Existing ultra-log-concavity/underdispersion and Poisson marginal entropy monotonicity do not resolve entropy vs the original count. The theorem proves a qualitative reversal for all fixed sample sizes and quantifies its exact high-rate cost; it is structurally informative, not a numerical table entry or elementary restatement.
